sentences.text: 4. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 322 of 2022, under Sections 376(D) of I.P.C. and Sections 5/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station - Karchhana, District - Prayagraj, during the pendency of trial.

PROSECUTION STORY:
5. The applicant and co-accused are stated to have outraged the modesty of the minor daughter of the informant aged about 14 years on 18.08.2022 at about 07:30 pm by taking her forcibly to an agricultural field.
6. The applicant is even stated to have attempted to commit rape with her by disrobing her.
7. The FIR was instituted on 31.08.2022 at about 09:19 pm.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
8. The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.
9. The FIR is delayed by about 11 days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
10. The medical examination of the victim has been delayed and it was taken up on 05.01.2022.
There is no injury observed by the doctor conducting the medical examination.
11. In the statement of the victim recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C., she has stated that aggravated sexual assault was committed with her by the applicant and co-accused person.

12. It is the prosecution story that they had dialed on the number 112, and the police reached and there is statement of the Sub-Inspector Mahesh Pandey, who has categorically stated that on being called, he had reached at place of occurrence and has found petty altercation between the parties.
13. The prosecution stands falsified by the statement of S.I. Mahesh Pandey.
14. The investigation was going on but subsequently under duress of the informant final report (charge sheet) has been submitted against the applicant and co-accused persons.
The applicant had surrendered before the court on 03.05.2024.
15. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.

16. The applicant is languishing in jail since 03.05.2024 having no criminal history to his credit,
deserves to be released on bail.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF INFORMANT:

sentences.text: The bail application has been vehemently opposed on the ground that the applicant kept on escaping the eyes of law and was absconding for a substantial period of 22 months and has surrendered on 03.05.2024 only, as such he is not entitled for bail.
18. The victim was minor aged about 14 years at the time of occurrence.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE:
19.
The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

CONCLUSION:
20. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

21. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
22.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view, the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595, has again emphasized that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
23.
Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
24. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

25. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, delay in institution of FIR, statement of S.I. Mahesh Yadav,
pending trial and considering the complicity of accused, severity of punishment, at this stage,
without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail. The bail application is allowed.

26. Let the applicant- Tej Bahadur, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Tej Bahadur vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51074651/
3 court concerned subject to following conditions.

entities.text: Tej Bahadur vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
27. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

28. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
